messages.author: a86dde8605b8eca8
messages.subject: Vectorization glmer2stan model
parts:
Hi everyone,
I'm a social science student who's currently learning STAN. I managed writing the models I need by altering some of the glmer2stan output, but they take very long to compute on my i7-3770, 16gb ram machine with Ubuntu 14.04. If someone finds a solution, I am happy if this will be put into the reference guide that Mr Betancourt wrote about in the consultation procedure thread. I see, that the program is not vectorized, but at the same time, I do not really understand how to vectorise it. 

My dependent variable is a test-outcome (0-5) and I have one independent variable (in other models more than two, but I think this does not matter too much, does it?) that should be partially pooled by groups (5 school types/ ~200schools/~400classes) and I want the intercept to be partially pooled, too.
Is it possible to use one predictor matrix for all independent variables, even though some effects vary by context and others don't? I haven't found an example where only some predictors vary by groups and others don't, so please apologise my naive questions
A run with 500 warmup iterations and 500 actual iterations took about 2 hours and the warmup phase took much longer than the other iterations.  Most parameters have converged however and have good effective sample sizes.

Below, you find the model. Sadly, I am not allowed to attach the data, as they will be released only later this year and are not completely anonymised yet. The speed does not vary a lot if I let the initial points to be random or 0. 

Thanks a lot!
Robert

data{
int N;
real grade[N];
real closure[N];
real age[N];
int girl[N];
int gen1[N];
int gen2[N];
int gen2_5[N];
int gen3[N];
real emplf[N];
real emplm[N];
real emplp[N];
real hisei[N];
int schtype[N];
int schoolid[N];
int classid[N];
int N_schtype;
int N_schoolid;
int N_classid;
}

transformed data{
vector[2] zeros_schtype;
vector[2] zeros_schoolid;
vector[2] zeros_classid;
for ( i in 1:2 ) zeros_schtype[i] <- 0;
for ( i in 1:2 ) zeros_schoolid[i] <- 0;
for ( i in 1:2 ) zeros_classid[i] <- 0;
}

parameters{
real Intercept;
real beta_closure;
real beta_age;
real beta_girl;
real beta_gen1;
real beta_gen2;
real beta_gen2_5;
real beta_gen3;
real beta_emplf;
real beta_emplm;
real beta_emplp;
real beta_hisei;
real<lower=0> sigma;
vector[2] vary_schtype[N_schtype];
vector<lower=0>[2] sigma_schtype;
corr_matrix[2] Rho_schtype;
vector[2] vary_schoolid[N_schoolid];
vector<lower=0>[2] sigma_schoolid;
corr_matrix[2] Rho_schoolid;
vector[2] vary_classid[N_classid];
vector<lower=0>[2] sigma_classid;
corr_matrix[2] Rho_classid;
}

transformed parameters{
cov_matrix[2] Sigma_schtype;
cov_matrix[2] Sigma_schoolid;
cov_matrix[2] Sigma_classid;
Sigma_schtype <- diag_matrix(sigma_schtype) * Rho_schtype * diag_matrix(sigma_schtype);
Sigma_schoolid <- diag_matrix(sigma_schoolid) * Rho_schoolid * diag_matrix(sigma_schoolid);
Sigma_classid <- diag_matrix(sigma_classid) * Rho_classid * diag_matrix(sigma_classid);
}

model{
real vary[N];
real glm[N];
// Priors
Intercept ~ normal(2.5 , 2 );
beta_closure ~ normal( 0 ,2 );
beta_age ~ normal( 0 , 2);
beta_girl ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_gen1 ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_gen2 ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_gen2_5 ~ normal( 0 ,2 );
beta_gen3 ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_emplf ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_emplm ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_emplp ~ normal( 0 , 2 );
beta_hisei ~ normal(0,2);
sigma_schtype ~ gamma( 2 , 1e-4 );
Rho_schtype ~ lkj_corr( 1.5 );
sigma_schoolid ~ gamma( 2 , 1e-4 );
Rho_schoolid ~ lkj_corr( 1.5 );
sigma_classid ~ gamma( 2 , 1e-4 );
Rho_classid ~ lkj_corr( 1.5 );
sigma ~ gamma( 2 , 1e-4 );
// Varying effects
for ( j in 1:N_schtype ) vary_schtype[j] ~ multi_normal( zeros_schtype , Sigma_schtype );
for ( j in 1:N_schoolid ) vary_schoolid[j] ~ multi_normal( zeros_schoolid , Sigma_schoolid );
for ( j in 1:N_classid ) vary_classid[j] ~ multi_normal( zeros_classid , Sigma_classid );
// Fixed effects
for ( i in 1:N ) {
vary[i] <- vary_schtype[schtype[i],1]
+ vary_schtype[schtype[i],2] * closure[i]
+ vary_schoolid[schoolid[i],1]
+ vary_schoolid[schoolid[i],2] * closure[i]
+ vary_classid[classid[i],1]
+ vary_classid[classid[i],2] * closure[i];
glm[i] <- vary[i] + Intercept
+ beta_closure * closure[i]
+ beta_age * age[i]
+ beta_girl * girl[i]
+ beta_gen1 * gen1[i]
+ beta_gen2 * gen2[i]
+ beta_gen2_5 * gen2_5[i]
+ beta_gen3 * gen3[i]
+ beta_emplf * emplf[i]
+ beta_emplm * emplm[i]
+ beta_emplp * emplp[i]
+ beta_hisei * hisei[i];
}
grade ~ normal( glm , sigma );
}

generated quantities{
real dev;
real vary[N];
real glm[N];
dev <- 0;
for ( i in 1:N ) {
vary[i] <- vary_schtype[schtype[i],1]
+ vary_schtype[schtype[i],2] * closure[i]
+ vary_schoolid[schoolid[i],1]
+ vary_schoolid[schoolid[i],2] * closure[i]
+ vary_classid[classid[i],1]
+ vary_classid[classid[i],2] * closure[i];
glm[i] <- vary[i] + Intercept
+ beta_closure * closure[i]
+ beta_age * age[i]
+ beta_girl * girl[i]
+ beta_gen1 * gen1[i]
+ beta_gen2 * gen2[i]
+ beta_gen2_5 * gen2_5[i]
+ beta_gen3 * gen3[i]
+ beta_emplf * emplf[i]
+ beta_emplm * emplm[i]
+ beta_emplp * emplp[i]
+ beta_hisei * hisei[i];
dev <- dev + (-2) * normal_log( grade[i] , glm[i] , sigma );
}
}'

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Re: Vectorization glmer2stan model
parts:
Robert:

First, glmer2stan is pretty much deprecated, to my mind, and I wrote it. Apologies for that. I'm just putting my programming time into my rethinking package, which is much more flexible. glmer2stan does still work, apparently. But I won't be updating it.

In any event, 2 hours to sample from a complex multilevel model with a lot of cases isn't so bad. Still, I bet there are low hanging fruit here, as the glmer2stan code is so old.

Some ideas to follow.

Re vectorization, it is mostly vectorized already. You can get a good amount of speedup from removing the varying effect loops. Change these lines:

for ( j in 1:N_schtype ) vary_schtype[j] ~ multi_normal( zeros_schtype , Sigma_schtype );
for ( j in 1:N_schoolid ) vary_schoolid[j] ~ multi_normal( zeros_schoolid , Sigma_schoolid );
for ( j in 1:N_classid ) vary_classid[j] ~ multi_normal( zeros_classid , Sigma_classid );

To:

vary_schtype ~ multi_normal( zeros_schtype , Sigma_schtype );
vary_schoolid ~ multi_normal( zeros_schoolid , Sigma_schoolid );
vary_classid ~ multi_normal( zeros_classid , Sigma_classid );

Second, I suspect those gamma priors on the sigma vectors are not particular helpful. But not knowing how many groups you have, I can't really say. You might try something tighter like cauchy(0,1) or cauchy(0,2), but sadly it all depends upon the scale of the data/parameters.

Third, the way covariance matrices are constructed can be improved. Change the lines:

Sigma_schtype <- diag_matrix(sigma_schtype) * Rho_schtype * diag_matrix(sigma_schtype);
Sigma_schoolid <- diag_matrix(sigma_schoolid) * Rho_schoolid * diag_matrix(sigma_schoolid);
Sigma_classid <- diag_matrix(sigma_classid) * Rho_classid * diag_matrix(sigma_classid);

I like the above, because it shows the actual calculation, but will be numerically better and certainly faster to change them to:

Sigma_schtype <- quad_form_diag( Rho_schtype , sigma_schtype );
Sigma_schoolid <- quad_form_diag( Rho_schoolid , sigma_schoolid );
Sigma_classid <- quad_form_diag( Rho_classid , sigma_classid );

All of that should provide a noticeable speedup. The Stan Team may chime in with some Matt trick advice. And you could squeeze out a little more speed by forming the data into a matrix and replacing the linear model loops with matrix algebra. 

But it doesn't sound like runs are really all that slow in the first place.

-Richard

parts:
Hi Richard,

thank you so much! I'll have a look at the rethinking package soon.
I'll change my code now and see whether it'll be faster. Regarding the group sizes: They are: school type 1: 50 schools, 95 classes, 1495 students, 
school type 2: 31 schools, 61 classes, 1335 students , school type 3: 19schools,  38classes, 784students, school type 4: 8schools, 14classes, 230students, school type 4: 22schools, 43classes, 985students. How does this affect the way that I should specify my priors?
Regarding the matrix algebra: I'm really a newbie with Stan and haven't used Jags or *Bugs extensively. Can I just specify a variable block for the variables that don't vary by context and have vectors for the variables which's effects vary by context? I tried that before but ended up with many errors (and I don't have the code anymore..). I couldn't find an example at the stan github page or elsewhere on the web.

Thank you so much for the kind and quick help!
Robert
